column1: # mapping_set_title: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 to Merged NIST AI RMF Schema Mappings

# mapping_set_description: Consolidated schema-level mappings from ISO/IEC 22989:2022 (Artificial intelligence concepts and terminology) to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework family of LinkML schemas (nist-ai-rmf umbrella plus its three modules nist-ai-100-1, nist-ai-600-1, and nist-ai-rmf-common). Use this file when a single rollup mapping is needed; per-module mappings live in iso22989-to-nist-ai-100-1.sssom.tsv, iso22989-to-nist-ai-600-1.sssom.tsv and iso22989-to-nist-ai-rmf-common.sssom.tsv.

column10: Shared identity root across the NIST AI RMF family.
NIST AI RMF reuses the ISO/IEC 22989 definition of an AI system.
ISO/IEC 22989 stakeholder role corresponds to NIST AI actor across all RMF modules.
Both partition the same AI lifecycle.
NIST AI RMF lifecycle stages follow the OECD lifecycle enumerated in ISO/IEC 22989 Annex A.
Same risk concept; nist-ai-600-1 GaiRisk is a generative-AI specialisation.
NIST GenAI risk is a specialisation of the ISO/IEC 22989 risk item.
ISO/IEC 22989 societal impact categories overlap with NIST harm categories.
Both enumerate bias categories relevant to AI systems; ISO/IEC 22989 follows ISO/IEC TR 24027.
ISO/IEC 22989 first-class class versus NIST AI RMF enumeration; same conceptual space.
Two enumerations cover the same trustworthiness characteristics with different granularities; see iso22989-to-nist-ai-rmf-common.sssom.tsv for per-value mappings.
Human-machine teaming addresses the GenAI human-AI-configuration risk category.
